steps.title: Fino
steps.body: Fino ages under flor, usually at least two years, often more, in Jerez or El Puerto. It's pale, bone dry, about 15%, with almond, bread dough, chamomile and a saline edge. El Puerto's Finos, closer to the sea, are often lighter. Fino is best fresh: once opened, drink within a few days.

steps.title: Manzanilla
steps.body: Manzanilla is Fino aged in Sanlúcar de Barrameda, at the mouth of the Guadalquivir. Cooler, more humid sea air keeps flor thicker all year, giving lighter, more saline, delicate wines with chamomile notes; manzanilla means chamomile in Spanish. Manzanilla Pasada is an older Manzanilla, with more nutty depth.

steps.prompt: Why is flor thicker in Sanlúcar de Barrameda?
steps.explanation: Sea air at the river mouth keeps flor thriving.

steps.title: En rama
steps.body: En rama, raw, means Sherry bottled with little or no filtration or fining, straight from the barrel. It's more intense and closer to the wine in the cask. Many bodegas release Fino and Manzanilla en rama seasonally, often in spring when flor is thickest. These are best drunk soon after bottling.
steps.highlight: En rama: unfiltered, from the cask

steps.title: What you learned
points: Fino ages under flor: pale, dry, almond and bread
Manzanilla is Sanlúcar's lighter, more saline Fino
En rama Sherries are unfiltered and best fresh
